newsitem.title: GERMANY: German March net borrowings at 1.5 bln dmk-Buba.
newsitem.headline: German March net borrowings at 1.5 bln dmk-Buba.

text.p: Although the German federal government again increased its gross borrowings considerably in March, net borrowings only totalled 1.5 billion marks, the Bundesbank said it its April report, released on Wednesday.

"In March the government's indebtedness on the capital markets was again very high totalling a gross 18 billion marks," the Bundesbank said. In February indebtedness on the capital markets totalled a gross 19 billion marks.

In March borrowings were offset by considerable redemptions, allowing net borrowing to total only 1.5 billion marks, the Bundesbank said, In February net borrowings were just under nine billion marks, the Bundesbank said.
For the entire first quarter, federal borrowing totalled 33.5 billion marks, with 12.5 billion marks borrowed in short-term funds.
Central, regional and local authorities borrowed 33.1 billion marks in January and February of this year, far above the 17.6 billion marks borrowed a year earlier.

Of the 33.1 billion mark total the federal government borrowed 30.8 billion marks in January and February, while the state governments borrowed 7.8 billion marks and the local governments borrowed 1.6 billion marks.
Only the local governments' borrowings were below last year's levels.
In January-February 1996, the federal government borrowed 13 billion marks, with the state governments borrowing 3.6 billion marks and the local governments borrowing two billion marks.
The redemption fund for inherited liabilities redeemed seven billion marks after having already paid back 3.5 billion marks in January. In January-February 1996 the fund borrowed 1.1 billion marks.

Foreign investors increased their holdings of domestic debt securities by 8.6 billion marks in February, which is considerably less than January's 31.2 billion marks worth of purchases. It is also slightly less than February 1996's 8.8 billion mark purchases.

Domestic investors in February purchased 24.8 billion marks of debt securities with credit institutions making up the bulk of that total with 22 billion marks. Non-banks purchased 2.8 billion marks, slightly more than the 1.4 billion marks purchased in February 1996.
